fact: The Minister of Education's Despacho 120/GME/2025, regulating the 2025/2026 school year for pre-school, basic and secondary education, orders at 2.12 that all Cabo Verdean schools in the national education system, public, semi-public and private, must adopt SIGE; it takes effect from 1 September 2025.

Despacho 120/GME/2025 orders at 2.11 that teachers must record the information from pupils' assessment electronically as well, on the result-entry sheets of the SIGE platform, where each teacher gets the final marks calculated by the legal formulas; it states an obligation for basic and secondary education in 2025/2026, not a measure of practice.
Despacho 120/GME/2025 obliges every school in the national system to adopt SIGE from the 2025/2026 school year and gives no count or share of schools that use it or enter data in it.

The Ministry of Education states that SIGE was piloted in 2009 in two secondary schools, spread from 2014, completed in all 43 secondary schools in July 2018, begun in compulsory basic education schools in September 2018 and completed in all 395 basic education schools in February 2019.

The Ministry of Education states that implementation of SIGE was concluded in February 2019 in all basic education schools of the country, 395 in total (395 of 395); the figure is of schools where it was implemented, not of schools entering data.

The Ministry of Education states that through the Dossier do Aluno, SIGE's link to the Porton di nos ilha portal, parents and guardians can check online a pupil's attendance, marks and fees and contact the school and teachers; the page gives no date for this, so the published date, inferred as February 2019, is used.

The Ministry of Education's own page states that SIGE was created by NOSi in partnership with the Ministry of Education to give the State a single school management system across the national territory, and that it lets the Ministry take decisions on results in good time; the page is undated, so the published date, inferred as February 2019, is used.

The Direção Nacional da Educação began national training on 15 July 2025 for inclusive-education team coordinators and the SIGE focal points of the municipalities on a new SIGE module for assessing children with special educational needs, built by the firm Devtrust.
The national director of education named UNICEF as strategic partner and main funder of the new SIGE special-needs assessment module, giving technical and financial support (15 July 2025).
The government's account of the eSkola launch on 25 June 2025 says SIGE is already used in all basic and secondary schools.
The government states that SIGE is 'already used in all' basic and secondary schools (25 June 2025); it gives no count of schools and no total, and says used, not how many enter data.

The eSkola app, fully integrated with SIGE and updated from it in real time, shows parents each pupil's timetable, test calendar, marks, absences and school history, so SIGE holds marks and absences per pupil during the year (25 June 2025).

The eSkola app on SIGE was launched by the national director of education on 25 June 2025; it was developed by the firm Devtrust, with which the Ministry of Education signed a cooperation protocol at the launch.

The education minister said about 200 teachers in 40 schools were under inspection for not entering pupils' marks in SIGE during a union-backed grade freeze, entry within the legal period being an obligation on teachers; the date is the article's, 1 June 2024, and no level or total of schools is given.

The October 2023 partnership compact lists among management gains the expansion of SIGE across the education system, integrating the country's basic (EBO) and secondary schools connected to the network, and gives its aim as one school management system in all basic and secondary schools; it does not itself describe what schools enter.

The compact's indicator 'share of schools with a functional SIGE reporting complete, quality data' has no baseline ('n.d.', reference year 2021) and a target of 100% for 2026; the same holds for kindergartens making their data available through SIGE (n.d., target 100%).

The compact, a Ministry of Education document, treats SIGE as the ministry's own system and commits to consolidating it and extending it to all subsystems, with 917 school heads and administrative staff and 600 kindergarten managers to be trained in its use by 2026.

The compact, aligned with the Plano Estratégico da Educação 2022-2026, names SIGE under 'data and evidence': consolidate and extend it to every subsystem, add variables notably on special educational needs, bring in private schools and link it to the single social registry and the civil registry.

The Plano Estratégico da Educação 2022-2026 (Ministry of Education, July 2023) names SIGE throughout: consolidating it as the sector's administrative and academic management platform, new modules including one on special educational needs, a ministerial order regulating its use, and costed activities such as 3 million escudos to extend it to pre-school and private schools.

The plan assigns SIGE's technical management, evolutionary maintenance and new modules to the ministry's Direção Geral da Comunicação, Tecnologia e Multimédia, with the Direção Nacional da Educação leading its use in schools and integration work involving NOSI (July 2023).

The plan lists a functional SIGE among the system's strengths and plans to reinforce its use in basic education units and increase its use in secondary schools; it records as a weakness that SIGE had not been put into effect in technical schools, and its extension to pre-school and technical education is still to come (July 2023).

The plan gives no figure for schools using SIGE in July 2023; it sets as results to be reached 'SIGE functional in all schools', 'functional at 100%', in full use by all teachers, and 98% of pre-school establishments and private schools using it.

The ministry's guidance for the 2023/2024 school year (July 2023) requires teachers to write the lesson summary and record absences daily in SIGE's digital class register during the lesson, to enter each assessment within 15 days, and to have all marks in SIGE at least 24 hours before the marks meetings; class directors complete each pupil's data and hold assessment meetings in SIGE.

The 2023/2024 guidance has retention decisions in the non-final years of basic education (2nd, 3rd and 5th) recorded in SIGE, and its SIGE chapter applies to school heads, teachers and class directors generally, with enrolment and attendance managed in SIGE; it does not separate basic from secondary schools (July 2023).

The guidance treats SIGE as in service across schools and gives no number of schools entering data; it orders all public, private and cooperative establishments to join SIGE during 2023/2024, at no extra cost (July 2023).

Under the ministry's new organic law SIGE passes to the Direção Nacional da Educação as a platform for pedagogical management, with the Direção Geral da Comunicação, Tecnologia e Multimédia providing technical support, and the ministry's municipal delegates acting as SIGE supervisors in place of the focal points whose role ended in 2021/2022 (guidance of July 2023).
